intro_lead_verbatim: The Hartwell Cardiovascular Innovation Forum 2026 brought companies, investors, clinicians and a regulator into one room for an afternoon, on the premise that those who fund, develop, regulate and use cardiovascular treatments rarely meet openly. The product closest to routine use was a device rather than a drug, and the clinicians on every panel returned to the same qualification: longer-acting treatment changes the burden of care without removing it.
intro_body_verbatim: Opening the meeting, Professor Annelise Dahlberg identified durability of lipid-lowering treatment as a challenge that "remains still a big challenge" and described inherited cardiomyopathy as an area "turning into real treatment options". The presentations that followed bore both statements out. Orrinvale Medical announced a CE mark for a leadless dual-chamber pacemaker; Halden Pharmaceuticals reported that its oral factor XI inhibitor had met its primary endpoint in a phase 3 trial of 11,400 patients; Vantrel Bio reported lipoprotein(a) lowering above 90% with an outcomes trial fully enrolled. Elsewhere the evidence was earlier: gene therapy for inherited cardiomyopathy rested on cohorts of 7 to 12 patients, and four of the eight emerging companies had no human data at all. The only regulator on the programme, Ilse Vandermeer, spoke in a personal capacity; the positions of regulators and payers were otherwise reported by companies and clinicians.

findings.headline_verbatim: A leadless dual-chamber pacing system is now CE-marked, and its use depends on catheterisation laboratory capacity and training.
findings.body_verbatim: Lena Fischer of Orrinvale Medical announced that the Orrinvale Duo received a CE mark on 22 September 2026, with an indication restricted to patients with atrioventricular block and preserved sinus function, and stated that the burden "shifts from the device clinic to the cath lab, it is not removed". In the pivotal DUET study of 415 patients, implant success was 98.3% and freedom from major complications at 12 months 94.1%, both shown on the slide. The figures that 95% of patients achieve atrioventricular synchrony and that 93% of physicians prefer the system were presented in a company video without reference to a named trial.

findings.headline_verbatim: Longer-acting treatment does not remove the requirement for ongoing monitoring.
findings.body_verbatim: Professor Sofia Esteves stated that no data support leaving a patient unseen for six months, and that in her reading of earlier data about half of patients in phase 2 needed uptitration; Professor Adaeze Nwosu stated that patients still need monitoring whatever the dosing interval. Miriam Castellanos of Arden Therapeutics did not propose a monitoring schedule for annual dosing. No speaker gave one.

findings.headline_verbatim: Lowering a biomarker is no longer accepted as sufficient evidence of benefit, and the UK health technology appraisal body wants hospitalisation reduction.
findings.body_verbatim: Professor Luís Figueiredo stated that the appraisal body wants a reduction in hospitalisation rather than a biomarker, and Nikolai Petrov of Fenwick Bio agreed that transthyretin knockdown will not be accepted as benefit on its own. These are accounts given by clinicians and companies, not statements by the body itself.
findings.notes: No numeric figures in the finding body. Footnote 2 contains dates from verification against the appraisal body's own listing (suspended since July 2025; nothing listed on 2 November 2026).

findings.headline_verbatim: One oral factor XI inhibitor has phase 3 data against a direct oral anticoagulant and a filing plan.
findings.body_verbatim: Owen Price of Halden Pharmaceuticals reported that in OSPREY-AF tabrexaban was noninferior to a standard direct oral anticoagulant for stroke or systemic embolism (hazard ratio 1.04, upper confidence bound 1.21 against a margin of 1.38), with major bleeding of 1.9% per year against 3.1%. He stated that the US regulator had given the company "a green light" to file on OSPREY-AF alone; this is the company's account of the regulator's position.

findings.headline_verbatim: Gene therapy for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is approaching pivotal planning; the phase 1/2 data show biomarker and mass changes, not outcomes.
findings.body_verbatim: Samuel Whitlock of Calderon Therapeutics reported that 12 patients had been dosed with CAL-201 in CALLISTO-HCM, with a 44% reduction in NT-proBNP at six months in the second cohort and no dose-limiting toxicities. A reduction in left ventricular mass index of 9 g/m2 appeared on the slide and was not spoken. The pivotal study is planned for the second half of 2027.

findings.headline_verbatim: First approvals in inherited cardiomyopathy were described as imminent, but each dated statement was a hope, a company target or a line on a slide.
findings.body_verbatim: Professor Robert Ashcroft stated that Harrowgate Therapeutics had announced positive pivotal results for a gene therapy in Fabry cardiomyopathy and that he "very much hopes" for approval early next year; nothing has been approved. Aisha Rahman of Ebbwater Genetics said EBW-100 "was approved for early access" in two countries, where the company's own slide describes a provisional authorisation with full authorisation pending.

findings.headline_verbatim: Peak oxygen uptake is being adopted as the pivotal endpoint in inherited cardiomyopathy, although many advanced patients cannot perform the test.
findings.body_verbatim: Grace Nakamura of Kessler Pharma reported a gain of 1.9 mL/kg/min against placebo in ORCHARD-HCM, and Felix Brandt of Oriel Cardiogenetics described a pivotal design on the same endpoint. Only 2 of the 9 patients in Oriel's LANTERNWAY study completed cardiopulmonary exercise testing.

findings.headline_verbatim: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the most contested inherited indication, and the figures for the oral drug in non-obstructive disease appeared only on the slide.
findings.body_verbatim: Nakamura stated that "about 10" interventional trials are running in the disease. The ORCHARD-1 result in non-obstructive disease, a gain of 0.8 mL/kg/min with p=0.238, was shown on the slide while the speaker described "a signal".

findings.headline_verbatim: Approval does not secure access, and one speaker reported that trial capacity is shrinking.
findings.body_verbatim: Laure Mercier of Lumavant stated that payers often require different study designs from regulators; Figueiredo cited a heart failure drug available in Switzerland without reimbursement. Daniel Kowalski of Fieldstone Clinical Research stated that the number of compounds in cardiovascular trials has risen "600%" in ten years while quality sites fall away.

findings.headline_verbatim: The European medicines regulator has not yet been asked to qualify an AI tool in cardiology, and its conditions are already specific.
findings.body_verbatim: Giving her personal views, Vandermeer stated that no major qualification request has come from cardiology and invited one; the conditions she set out for AI in trial analysis were a frozen model, a frozen data pipeline, pre-specified validation and a clinically relevant endpoint. She put the number of scientific advice procedures involving AI in 2025 at "maybe 12".

findings.headline_verbatim: The one patient who spoke defined success as not getting worse, and did not expect permanence.
findings.body_verbatim: Mateus Oliveira, 27, treated with a gene therapy about three years ago, said he had been told at 19 that he would need a transplant, that he can now climb the stairs at university "without stopping on the landing", and that he hopes the treatment "has bought me 10 to 15 years". He did not name the product and gave no clinical measurements.

footnotes.text_verbatim: The summary slide shown after the video states "> 90%" for both figures; the video gives 95% and 93%. Neither names a trial.

On review, the appraisal body's own listing shows its appraisal of a transthyretin silencer from another company as suspended since July 2025; no active appraisal of a medicine for amyloid cardiomyopathy was listed on 2 November 2026. The panel described the position as "in process".
The slide gives only "filing planned 1Q 2027". The statement about the regulator was spoken and does not appear on any slide or in any public source found on review.
The speaker said "nearly half"; the slide gives 43.8%.
The slide gives the readout as "2H 2027". The speaker said "over 90%" for the phase 2 reduction; the slide gives 94%.
The slide reads "provisional authorisation under an early-access framework; full authorisation pending". The spoken word "approved" overstates it.
A conference report found on review gives the p value as 0.20; the slide gives 0.238. Neither is statistically significant.
His own chart runs from about 20 compounds to about 120, nearer 500%. His slides were marked confidential.
The "10 to 15 years" is his expectation, not time already gained; he added "I don't know if it's forever".
